articles.title: Preços da Black Friday: Itens dobram de valor em 24h, aponta g1 | G1
articles.standfirst: Levantamento começou em agosto e será atualizado até a Black Friday, na próxima sexta-feira (27). Nesta terça, 39 produtos estavam abaixo do preço médio do período; 28 estão mais caros.
articles.summary: O monitoramento de preços da Black Friday do g1 identificou que 28 de 74 itens subiram de valor, com casos de produtos que ficaram duas vezes mais caros em 24 horas.
articles.body:
Aumento de preço em produto na semana da Black Friday; g1 monitora preços desde agosto. — Foto: g1

Até a Black Friday, na sexta-feira (27), o Guia de Compras vai mostrar, a cada dia útil, como estão os preços de 74 produtos monitorados pelo g1 desde agosto.

Metade do dobro? Nesta terça-feira (24), alguns dos produtos que lideravam em descontos no início da semana sofreram aumentos significativos de preços, com exemplos de valores até duas vezes mais caros que na segunda-feira (23) .

Os valores são referentes ao preço no cartão e não consideram descontos no Pix. Veja os produtos mais afetados entre segunda e terça-feira:

Air Fryer WAP Multi-Comb 16L : de R$ 499 a R$ 809;

Ar-condicionado LG 14.000 BTUs : de R$ 5.186 a R$ 6.599;

Galaxy A17 5G 128 GB : de R$ 959 a R$ 1.175,29;

Lava-louças Electrolux 14 Serviços : de R$ 4.139 a R$ 5.038.

No total, 28 dos 74 itens estão hoje mais caros do que a média desde agosto. É aí que mora o risco: se um produto sobe agora e cai na Black Friday, o “desconto” pode só devolvê-lo ao preço de antes.

Por outro lado, 39 dos 74 produtos estavam mais baratos do que a média desde agosto . Desses, somente 7 tiveram mais de 10% de desconto, três a menos do que na segunda-feira (23) . A maioria ficou entre 1% e 6%.

O produto com o maior desconto do dia é o celular Oppo Reno 16F 256GB, por R$ 3.599 (-16%). A maior alta é do ar-condicionado Philco PAC12000QF5 12.000 BTUs, por R$ 5.164,47 (+56%).

O g1 vai acompanhar esses itens para mostrar se isso acontece. A página será atualizada em todos os dias de semana (exceto fins de semana).

É o terceiro ano seguido em que o Guia de Compras faz o levantamento, com base em buscas regulares nas principais lojas da internet. A lista inclui as categorias mais procuradas nesta época, como celulares, TVs, eletrodomésticos, eletroportáteis e videogames.

Como usar o comparador de preços do Guia de Compras?

Na página do item, um gráfico de variação de preços mostra de forma rápida os momentos em que o produto esteve mais caro e as datas em que atingiu os menores valores.

Escolha o modelo do produto em que você está de olho.

Na página inicial, você pode visualizar o produto pela faixa de desconto (5%, 10%, 15%) ou selecionar a categoria desejada (ex: Cozinha).

Também é possível consultar uma tabela completa com todas as cotações registradas entre agosto e o momento atual.

articles.title: Associação de produtores rurais diz não reconhecer como representante o antropólogo detido no PA em operação do Ibama | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo Pedro Pintado, presidente da Asprub, não há relação entre as partes. Edward Luz diz que tem sondado a possibilidade, mas até agora nada foi formalizado.
articles.summary: Segundo Pedro Pintado, presidente da Asprub, não há relação entre as partes. Edward Luz diz que tem sondado a possibilidade, mas até agora nada foi formalizado.
articles.body:
A Associação dos Produtores Rurais e Agro-industrial do Vale do Bacajaí (Asprub) disse que não reconhece o antropólogo Edward Luz como representante. O pesquisador foi detido ao tentar impedir uma ação do Ibama no sudoeste do Pará. Em entrevista ao G1 , o presidente da associação, Pedro Pintado, disse que , apesar de conhecer o antropólogo, Edward nunca fez parte do grupo.

Homem é detido por fiscais do Ibama ao tentar impedir fiscalização em terra indígena no Pará — Foto: Reprodução Twitter/edwardluz

Em documento divulgado e assinado por Luz, ele seria consultor da associação e alegou ter participado da reunião que definiu acordo com o Ibama para suspender a retirada de famílias em situação de vulnerabilidade social em uma região não reservada no sudoeste do Pará. Nem Edward Luz e nem a Asprub são citados na ata da reunião que discutiu as operações do Ibama na região.

Antropólogo Edward Luz distribuiu folheto informando que representava a Asprub na região do Ituna, Itatá e Bacajá, no Pará — Foto: Reprodução/TV Liberal

De acordo com Pedro Pintado, presidente há 12 anos da associação, não há relação entre as partes. "Sou muito amigo dele (antropólogo), mas ele nunca prestou serviço para a Asprub. Ele não representa nenhum associado nosso e não prestou serviço para a Asprub", afirma.

Em entrevista ao G1 , o antropólogo informou que está atuando principalmente com a Associação dos Produtores Rurais e Agroindustriais do Vale do Bacajai e Região (Apravb), que também ocupa a área onde está sendo demarcar a Terra Indígena Ituna-Itatá, e confirmou que não é representante legal da Asprub, mas está em tratativas contratuais e que presta consultoria voluntária.

"Desde o começo de toda esta situação eu venho mantendo tratativas contratuais com os presidentes de associações dos dois assentamentos (Itatá e Lages), com o senhor Antônio Gonçalves de Lima, presidente da Apravb e com o senhor Pedro Pintado, presidente da Asprub. Apesar da amizade desenvolvida e das conversações mantidas com a Asprub, de fato, ainda não foi formalizado nenhum contrato de prestação de serviços com esta associação. Não obstante, este fato, é mais do que evidente que os serviços de consultoria antropológica prestado à Apravb beneficiarão também os associados a Asprub. Trata-se portanto de mera filigrana contratual ainda não resolvida", diz Edward Luz.

"Nós temos conversado, minha colaboradora já conversou com ele (Pedro Pintado - Asprub), solicitado informações, sondado a possibilidade de ver qualquer contrato, mas até agora nada foi formalizado, nada foi nesse sentido. Nós temos trabalhado em parceria, temos trabalhado em uma consultoria voluntária, que certamente beneficiará os assentados da Asprub, mas nada foi formalizado aqui", completou.

Edward Luz foi detido após tentar barrar uma ação do Ibama e se recusar a deixar área da terra indígena. Luz, que disse prestar consultoria para produtores rurais da região, foi liberado no mesmo dia. Ao ser abordado pelos fiscais, ele alegou que as fiscalizações haviam sido suspensas pelo ministro do Meio Ambiente, Ricardo Salles. O ministro, por sua vez, disse não conhecer o homem e defendeu a ação do instituto.

Imagem de fiscalização do Ibama na terra indígena Ituna-Itatá em 21 de janeiro de 2020 mostra sinais de desmatamento ilegal. — Foto: Divulgação/Ibama

Apesar de ser considerada uma Terra Indígena, a região do Ituna-Itatá, local onde o antropólogo Edward Luz foi detido, ainda está em processo de transição para ser demarcado efetivamente como área de proteção de povos indígenas.

"Lá tem Terra Indígena demarcada, ou seja, acabou o processo e já é TI. E tem uma área menor, que faz parte de um ato da Funai, que chama interdição, que é quando você tem a possibilidade de ter índios isolados e aí você separa a área, deixa ela reservada para depois utilizar ela na criação de uma TI, se for confirmada a existência de índios isolados. Ou seja, a área reservada é a que tem interdição pela possibilidade de haver povos indígenas", explica o procurador Daniel Azeredo, do Ministério Publico Federal (MPF).

No entanto, apesar de legalmente a área ainda não ser considerada uma Terra Indígena, não há justificativa para o aumento do desmatamento constatado na área, que bateu recorde em 2019 . O Procurador alerta que a região é de propriedade da União e, portanto, não poderia abrigar assentamentos.

"Lá é uma área com índice de desmatamento altíssimo, principalmente de 2018 pra cá. Isso implica dois fatores para a ação do Ibama. Mesmo não sendo uma TI, a região compreende terras públicas, da União, que precisam ser protegidas. Além do mais, mesmo que fossem áreas privadas, o desmatamento não pode acontecer como está acontecendo lá. Tem um dano ambiental lá muito grande", afirmou.

Terra indígena Ituna-Itatá, no Pará — Foto: Rodrigo Sanches/G1

articles.title: Justiça absolve e solta vendedor que ficou 89 dias preso por engano em SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Na sentença de absolvição, juiz considerou as contradições apresentadas pelos policiais militares nas audiências e constatou que Wanderson Brandão, 23, não poderia estar nos locais do assalto.
articles.summary: Na sentença de absolvição, juiz considerou as contradições apresentadas pelos policiais militares nas audiências e constatou que Wanderson Brandão, 23, não poderia estar nos locais do assalto.
articles.body:
O vendedor Wanderson Gomes Brandão, 23 anos, foi absolvido e solto pela Justiça nesta segunda-feira (17) depois de ter ficado 89 dias preso por engano no Centro de Detenção Provisória (CDP) de Guarulhos, na Grande São Paulo. A sentença é do juiz Antonio Maria Patiño Zorz, da 29ª Vara Criminal de São Paulo.

Segundo o Monitor da Violência , levantamento feito pelo G1 e divulgado nesta quarta (19), a superlotação de presídios no país registrou leve queda . A redução no número de presos sem condenação aliviou a pressão do último ano, mas as prisões ainda estão 68% acima da capacidade.

Considerando o número absoluto de presos, o Brasil ocupa a 3ª posição, atrás apenas de China e Estados Unidos.

Wanderson foi preso em 21 de novembro de 2019, durante uma abordagem de policiais militares na Vila Campestre, no Jabaquara, na Zona Sul de São Paulo. Segundo os policiais, Wanderson teria participado do roubo seguido de dois carros no bairro, junto com outros três rapazes.

"Ainda não caiu a ficha, ainda acho que estou preso. Nunca quis roubar ninguém, nunca quis isso para minha vida. Agora, depois do que passei na cadeia tenho a certeza de que continuarei não querendo roubar ninguém", disse Wanderson ao G1 .

Segundo os policiais militares, o primeiro roubo aconteceu perto da Rua das Rolinhas, no mesmo bairro. O crime teria sido cometido por "Wanderson e outros três indivíduos desconhecidos, mediante violência e grave ameaça consistente na simulação de emprego de arma de fogo exercida contra as vítimas (...), tentaram subtrair para eles, bens pessoais das vítimas, não se consumando por circunstâncias alheias as suas vontades."

De acordo com a versão das vítimas, Wanderson teria assumido o volante do carro e saído em alta velocidade. Instantes depois, eles teriam abordado um casal em um outro carro na mesma região. Os PMs informaram que iniciaram uma perseguição policial por cerca de 15 minutos, até encontrar Wanderson e outros três rapazes. Eles foram levados para a delegacia pare reconhecimento.

As vítimas fizeram o reconhecimento apenas de Wanderson e a prisão em flagrante dele foi convertida em prisão preventiva. Na audiência de custódia, uma das vítimas negou o reconhecimento de Wanderson.

Luzinete abraça o filho Wanderson após ele ser absolvido pela Justiça da acusação de roubo de dois carros — Foto: Glauco Araújo/G1

"Só levaram em consideração a palavra da vítima do roubo, não levaram em conta a palavra de meu filho, que nunca teve passagem na polícia, tem ficha limpa, estava trabalhando como faz desde os 14 anos, no mesmo lugar, perto de casa. Eles não levaram em conta, por exemplo, que meu filho não sabe dirigir, nunca pegou um carro. Como ele poderia ter roubado e dirigido o carro da vítima?", disse Luzinete Gomes Brandão, mãe de Wanderson.

Os policiais militares disseram que foram acionados pelo Copom sobre o roubo dos dois carros. Eles afirmaram terem participado da perseguição aos criminosos, que escaparam por um favela.

Câmera de segurança mostra Wanderson saindo de casa no mesmo horário que policiais militares afirmaram que ele teria cometido dois assaltos na Zona Sul de São Paulo — Foto: Glauco Araújo/G1

O juiz considerou contraditórios os depoimentos dos dois policiais. No caso de um deles, ele disse que "ainda, que entre a parada e a abordagem a distância era de mais ou menos cinco metros. Por fim, aduziu que o acusado negou os fatos, aduzindo que estava no serviço dele, bem próximo dali."

No texto da sentença, o juiz citou que um dos policiais disse que "entre a parada e o abandono do veículo até a abordagem do réu se passaram cerca de seis ou sete minutos, tendo o réu negado os fatos na abordagem, aduzindo que trabalhava em uma loja de rações."

O juiz Antonio Zorz concluiu a sentença afirmando que é "inegável que houve a ação de quatro agentes que consumaram o roubo de um veículo e na sequência tentaram subtrair outro veículo em que estava um casal. Contudo, se há certeza dos crimes, o mesmo não se pode dizer em relação à autoria."

"Como dito, se a prova indiciária parecia apontar com certeza a atuação do réu, em juízo a prova da autoria foi colocada em dúvida. Não obstante o reconhecimento do réu por duas das três vítimas em juízo, a prova produzida durante a instrução processual se encontra permeada de desencontros que não permitem um desfecho condenatório, porquanto suficientes para incutir neste juízo razoável dúvida quanto à autoria", disse o juiz Antonio Zorz.

O texto do juiz ainda citou que "a primeira incoerência revelada durante a instrução, e que informa o reconhecimento realizado por parte das vítimas, é a absoluta e gritante divergência encontrada entre os relatos dos policiais ouvidos em juízo, vez que enquanto a testemunha, policial militar, relatou que durante a perseguição policial perdeu os roubadores de vista por cerca de apenas alguns segundos e por mínima distância (cerca de cinco metros) até a abordagem, a testemunha policial, componente da mesma guarnição, relatou que perdeu de vista os bandidos por cerca de 6 ou 7 minutos!!"

Local onde Wanderson foi abordado pelos policiais militares fica a menos de 50 metros de casa e do trabalho, no Jabaquara, na Zona Sul de São Paulo — Foto: Glauco Araújo/G1

O magistrado desconsiderou a versão dos policiais militares por conta da fragilidade das informações relatadas por eles.

"E tal detalhe não pode passar despercebido, pois a considerar a versão de um dos policiais, a toda evidência, a consequência lógica é que o réu era de fato um dos ocupantes do carro abandonado, pois a distância e os segundos de perseguição permitiriam tal conclusão. De outra parte, a considerar o quanto dito pelo policial, conclui-se que todos a abordagem do réu não se deu por uma perseguição certeira e imediata e sim pelas características físicas e vestes do réu, o que vem fortalecer a tese da defesa, mormente em consideração à prova testemunhal defensiva produzida."

Antonio Zorz disse ainda, na sentença, que "nesta linha de raciocínio, começa a se questionar o motivo pelo qual tal agente sequer fora identificado pelas características físicas pelos ofendidos! (...) A testemunha [PM] ainda relatou que não reconheceu o réu como sendo o indivíduo abordado na comunidade, trazendo mais dúvidas ainda sobre a dinâmica real em que se deu a abordagem do acusado, o que começa a comprometer a certeza outrora advinda da prova indiciária."

Para reforçar a defesa de Wanderson, o advogado Anderson Costa e Silva apresentou o laudo do GPS do celular de Wanderson, mostrando que o aparelho permaneceu todo o tempo em que ocorreram os dois roubos na casa e no trabalho do réu. Além disso, uma câmera de segurança mostra que Wanderson estava em sua casa quando os roubos ocorriam.

"Quero Justiça, quero que todos os envolvidos em me colocar na cadeia paguem pelo que fizeram. Eu paguei por algo que não fiz. O que eu vivi na cadeia eu nunca imaginei que passaria um dia. Quero meu nome limpo, quero poder andar na rua sem medo. Eu sei que sou inocente", disse Wanderson.

Em resumo, o juiz afirma que "de um lado o reconhecimento efetuado pelos ofendidos que contrasta com uma diligência não certeira dos policiais de uma mesma viatura, acrescido de testemunhas de defesa que vieram ofertar álibi ao réu, além da comprovação de imagem e GPS de aparelho que indicam que o réu não poderia estar nos locais do assalto."

"Ainda tem justiça a ser feita. Parte da justiça foi feita, mas ainda falta responsabilizar quem colocou meu filho inocente na cadeia, fazer ele passar pelo que passou, pelo que minha família passou", disse Luzinete em defesa do filho.

Wanderson deixou o CDP de Guarulhos nesta segunda-feira (17) após a Justiça absolvê-lo em processo que o acusava de dois roubos na Zona Sul de SP — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

articles.summary: Bom dia! Aqui estão os principais assuntos para você começar o dia bem-informado.
articles.body:
O número de presos sem condenação diminui no país, e a superlotação nos presídios tem leve melhora. Segundo levantamento do Monitor da Violência, a taxa de detentos provisórios caiu de 36% para 31% desde abril, mas prisões estão 68% acima da capacidade . Veja os dados da ferramenta exclusiva do G1 , análises, o mapa da superlotação e a posição do Brasil no ranking mundial de presos por habitantes. O podcast O Assunto explica como o ICMS virou briga política. Justiça do Trabalho suspende demissões e greve de petroleiros pode estar chegando ao fim. Reforma da Previdência de SP é aprovada em 1º turno. E veja os números grandiosos do carnaval de rua pelo país.

O Monitor da Violência traz hoje um Raio X sobre o sistema prisional do Brasil. O levantamento mostra que a superlotação diminuiu e o percentual de presos provisórios no país é o menor dos últimos anos . Mas 31% dos detentos ainda aguardam julgamento. Os dados mostram ainda que o país tem 388 encarcerados a cada 100 mil habitantes . A análise traz também um balanço do número de mulheres grávidas ou com filho pequeno que deixaram a prisão nos últimos dois anos.

ICMS: como o imposto virou briga política . O imposto têm grande peso na arrecadação dos Estados e colocou governadores e presidente em lados opostos. Para entender a importância do ICMS nas contas estaduais, como o imposto surgiu e o que está por trás dessa disputa, Renata Lo Prete conversa com Valdo Cruz, da TV Globo em Brasília, e com a economista Ana Carla Abrão. Ouça:

Petroleiros fazem atos em Pernambuco durante greve nacional da categoria — Foto: Sindipetro / Divulgação

A desembargadora Rosalie Michaele Bacila Batista, do Tribunal Regional do Trabalho (TRT) da 9ª Região, suspendeu a demissão dos trabalhadores da subsidiária da Petrobras Araucária Nitrogenados (Ansa), em Araucária , na Região Metropolitana de Curitiba. articles.standfirst: A explosão de um carro-bomba na segunda-feira (23), em Villavicencio, no centro da Colômbia, causou grandes danos à sede do governo regional e provocou cenas de caos, às vésperas dos dez anos da assinatura do acordo de paz com a principal guerrilha do país.

articles.body:
A explosão de um carro-bomba na segunda-feira (23), em Villavicencio, no centro da Colômbia, causou grandes danos à sede do governo regional e provocou cenas de caos, às vésperas dos dez anos da assinatura do acordo de paz com a principal guerrilha do país.

O atentado deixou cerca de 20 feridos, segundo a imprensa local.

Imagens capturadas por moradores do vilarejo e por câmeras de segurança registraram o momento da explosão. É possível ouvir um forte estrondo e ver uma bola de fogo se formando enquanto carros passam. Em outro vídeo, um morador capturou uma grande nuvem de fumaça no local do atentado.

Nuvem de fumaça é vista no céu da cidade de Villavicencio, na região central da Colômbia, em 23 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Reprodução/ Redes sociais

➡️ O ataque ocorre em um momento em que o presidente Abelardo de la Espriella, no poder desde 7 de agosto, conduz uma ofensiva militar, com apoio dos Estados Unidos, contra grupos armados que financiam suas atividades com receitas do tráfico de cocaína. O país enfrenta a pior onda de violência em uma década.

"O narcoterrorismo está desesperado porque o combatemos com determinação. Ele tenta nos intimidar e nos obrigar a recuar", declarou o presidente na noite de segunda-feira, em uma publicação na rede X.

A bomba explodiu pouco depois das 21h (2h de terça-feira, pelo horário de Brasília), abrindo uma enorme cratera no local. Até o momento, não há registro de mortes.

O centro da cidade ficou sem energia elétrica. A explosão provocou cenas de pânico, com moradores correndo pelas ruas em meio a destroços e fachadas danificadas, segundo jornalistas da AFP que estavam no local.

Um homem e uma mulher estão ao lado de uma área danificada após a explosão de uma bomba nas proximidades da sede do governo do departamento de Meta, em Villavicencio, na Colômbia, em 23 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: AFP - MARIO TORO

Johan Pérez, proprietário de uma loja de chapéus, foi surpreendido pela explosão, ocorrida na praça principal de Villavicencio. "Portas foram arrombadas, vidros quebrados e algumas vitrines internas explodiram", contou à AFP, com a voz embargada. "É um milagre estarmos vivos."

Segundo o presidente colombiano, a bomba tinha como alvo a sede do governo do departamento de Meta.

A imprensa local informa que cerca de 20 pessoas ficaram feridas. As autoridades ainda não divulgaram um balanço oficial.

"Aviso aos narcoterroristas responsáveis: este atentado não ficará impune", afirmou Abelardo de la Espriella, que sucedeu em agosto o ex-presidente de esquerda Gustavo Petro e defende uma política de linha dura contra os grupos criminosos.

"Inaceitável e doloroso. Até onde querem nos levar? Semear o medo é fácil. Construir e reconstruir: é isso que fazem os corajosos", declarou na rede X a defensora pública Iris Marin.

Dez anos do acordo com as Farc O ataque de segunda-feira ocorreu na véspera do décimo aniversário da assinatura do acordo de paz entre o Estado colombiano e as Farc (Forças Armadas Revolucionárias da Colômbia), a guerrilha mais poderosa do continente.

Na região atingida pelo atentado atua uma dissidência da antiga organização, que rejeitou o acordo histórico e atualmente disputa com outros grupos os lucros da mineração ilegal e do tráfico de drogas na Colômbia, maior produtor mundial de cocaína.

Até o momento, nenhum grupo reivindicou a autoria do ataque em Villavicencio. Pouco antes da explosão, De la Espriella havia criticado duramente os custos do acordo de paz, assinado em 24 de novembro de 2016, e o classificou como uma "falsa paz".

Em entrevista à AFP por ocasião dos dez anos do acordo, Ingrid Betancourt, figura mais conhecida entre as vítimas de sequestros realizados pelas Farc, avaliou que o tratado "não cumpriu suas promessas".

Este é o segundo atentado registrado na Colômbia em menos de 24 horas. Mais cedo, na segunda-feira, um ataque com drones — equipamentos frequentemente utilizados por grupos criminosos contra policiais e civis — deixou três feridos, incluindo um menor de idade, em Cúcuta, cidade na fronteira com a Venezuela.

Entre janeiro e novembro, o país registrou 358 ataques com drones carregados de explosivos, segundo um documento do Ministério da Defesa consultado na segunda-feira pela AFP.

articles.title: A cantora iraniana que levou 74 chicotadas por cantar sem hijab | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo relatos, Parastoo Ahmadi, três músicos e um produtor receberam as chicotadas na cidade de Qom.
articles.summary: Segundo relatos, Parastoo Ahmadi, três músicos e um produtor receberam as chicotadas na cidade de Qom.
articles.body:
A apresentação de Parastoo Ahmadi foi transmitida ao vivo em seu canal no YouTube em dezembro de 2024. — Foto: Reprodução/Youtube

Uma cantora que se apresentou sem o hijab obrigatório no Irã e quatro integrantes de sua banda e equipe de produção foram açoitados pelas autoridades iranianas, segundo os advogados dos artistas.

Parastoo Ahmadi, três músicos e um produtor receberam, cada um, 74 chibatadas na cidade de Qom, informou à BBC News um integrante da equipe de defesa.

Ahmadi, de 29 anos, usou um vestido sem mangas durante um show transmitido ao vivo pela internet em dezembro de 2024. As leis do Irã proíbem apresentações públicas de mulheres e exigem que elas usem véus cobrindo a cabeça e roupas discretas.

Em junho deste ano, um tribunal criminal de Qom condenou Ahmadi e outras oito pessoas por "atentar contra a decência pública" por meio da publicação de "material obsceno e indecente", acusações que eles negaram.

Eles também foram proibidos de exercer atividades audiovisuais e de deixar o país por dois anos.

No fim de setembro, um tribunal de apelação em Qom rejeitou o recurso dos réus e confirmou a sentença, segundo seus advogados.

As condenações foram amplamente criticadas por outros artistas iranianos e ativistas dos direitos humanos, que alertaram que açoitamento constitui uma punição cruel, desumana e degradante, além de violar a proibição internacional da tortura.

Na segunda-feira (23/11), um dos advogados dos réus disse à BBC que Ahmadi e quatro de seus funcionários haviam recebido as chibatadas na terceira seção do Departamento de Execução de Sentenças Criminais de Qom.

"Fizemos tudo o que estava ao nosso alcance para anular a sentença ou, pelo menos, conseguir uma redução da pena ou sua suspensão, mas não tivemos sucesso", afirmou. "Os outros advogados e eu tentamos até mesmo adiar a execução da sentença, mas o departamento responsável por sua aplicação insistiu em colocá-la em prática imediatamente."

O jornal reformista Etemad citou outro advogado de defesa, Mostafa Nili, que identificou os quatro homens açoitados ao lado de Ahmadi como Soheil Faghih-Nasiri, Amin Taheri, Amirali Pirnia e Mohsen Lashkari.

"Açoitarem Parastoo Ahmadi por cantar e se vestir como ela quer é uma violação flagrante de seus direitos fundamentais e uma demonstração assustadora da determinação das autoridades iranianas em reprimir a liberdade das mulheres e punir violentamente qualquer pessoa que ouse desafiar suas leis e políticas discriminatórias", afirmou Bahar Ghandehari, diretora de defesa de direitos do Centro pelos Direitos Humanos no Irã (CHRI), com sede nos Estados Unidos.

De acordo com a legislação iraniana, baseada na interpretação da lei islâmica adotada pelo país, mulheres e meninas que já atingiram a puberdade devem cobrir os cabelos com o hijab e usar roupas longas e folgadas que escondam as formas do corpo.

Em 2022, uma onda de protestos tomou conta da República Islâmica após a morte sob custódia de Mahsa Amini, uma mulher curda de 22 anos detida pela polícia da moralidade em Teerã, em setembro daquele ano, por supostamente usar o hijab de maneira "inadequada".

Mulheres queimaram seus véus ou os ergueram no ar durante as manifestações em todo o país contra as regras clericais. Centenas de pessoas foram mortas durante a repressão promovida pelas forças de segurança.

Desde então, muitas mulheres e meninas deixaram de cobrir os cabelos em público, desafiando abertamente o código de vestimenta. As autoridades responderam com ondas periódicas de prisões , advertências, fechamento de estabelecimentos comerciais e outras medidas.

Em janeiro deste ano, milhares de pessoas foram mortas e dezenas de milhares foram presas quando as forças de segurança reprimiram uma nova onda de protestos em massa contra o regime, desta vez motivada pela crise econômica do país.

Desde o início da guerra do Irã com os EUA e Israel, no fim de fevereiro, as autoridades intensificaram o uso da pena de morte contra manifestantes.

Segundo a organização Iran Human Rights, sediada na Noruega, ao menos 39 homens condenados em razão dos protestos de janeiro e outros dois condenados por sua participação nas manifestações de 2022 foram executados.

Também foram executadas 16 pessoas supostamente ligadas a grupos de oposição proibidos e outras 17 condenadas por espionagem ou colaboração com os EUA.

Outros 121 manifestantes detidos em janeiro, incluindo seis mulheres e cinco menores de idade, foram condenados à morte e correm risco de execução, afirma a organização.

articles.title: Arquiteto do 'Terror Vermelho' soviético é homenageado em Moscou | G1
articles.standfirst: Felix Dzerzhinsky lançou as bases do sistema repressivo que viria a ser presidido por Josef Stalin. Ele é criticado pelas dezenas de milhares de execuções sumárias praticadas pela polícia secreta bolchevique.
articles.summary: Felix Dzerzhinsky lançou as bases do sistema repressivo que viria a ser presidido por Josef Stalin.
articles.body:
Agentes das forças de segurança passam por uma placa memorial recém-inaugurada em homenagem a Félix Dzerjinski, fundador da polícia secreta soviética, em Moscou, na Rússia, em 23 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Ramil Sitdikov/Reuters

Felix Dzerzhinsky, fundador da polícia secreta soviética e arquiteto do "Terror Vermelho" que se seguiu à Revolução Russa, recebeu uma placa comemorativa em Moscou que o descreve como um "estadista notável" — para o deleite dos nacionalistas de linha-dura.

Dzerzhinsky, um nobre polonês que se tornou revolucionário e lançou as bases do sistema repressivo que viria a ser presidido por Josef Stalin , é criticado por muitos pelas dezenas de milhares de execuções sumárias que sua Cheka realizou para consolidar o poder bolchevique entre 1918 e 1922.

Mas, para muitos no aparato de segurança que exerce enorme influência na Rússia do presidente Vladimir Putin, Dzerzhinsky é um herói e um símbolo poderoso de um Estado que depende fortemente do FSB — a organização sucessora da KGB soviética e que já foi dirigida por Putin.

A grande placa de bronze, que o retrata de terno tendo como pano de fundo chaminés de fábricas, um trem a vapor e um poste de alta tensão, foi colocada em um prédio onde Dzerzhinsky trabalhou de 1924 a 1926, não muito longe do Kremlin. Ela o exalta como o iniciador da industrialização em grande escala que transformou a economia soviética nos primeiros anos.

Placa memorial recém-inaugurada em homenagem a Félix Dzerjinski, fundador da polícia secreta soviética, em Moscou, na Rússia, em 23 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Ramil Sitdikov/Reuters

Dzerzhinsky, cuja estátua no centro de Moscou foi derrubada como símbolo de repressão quando a União Soviética caiu há mais de três décadas, teve o que os críticos consideram um retorno perturbador nos últimos anos, parte do que eles dizem ser uma iniciativa das autoridades para reabilitá-lo, ao mesmo tempo em que minimizam os momentos mais sombrios da história do país, em um momento em que a Rússia está em um impasse com o Ocidente por causa da guerra na Ucrânia.

Em abril, Putin ordenou que a academia de espionagem russa FSB voltasse a adotar seu nome da era soviética em homenagem a Dzerzhinsky; o serviço de inteligência externa russo SVR revelou uma estátua dele em sua sede em Moscou em 2023; e estátuas dele foram erguidas nas cidades de Omsk e Vladivostok no ano passado.

Vladimir Medinsky, assessor de Putin que liderou as delegações russas nas negociações de paz com a Ucrânia, foi um dos políticos que inaugurou a nova placa na última sexta-feira (20)

Medinsky, autor de alguns dos novos livros didáticos de história da Rússia, elogiou Dzerzhinsky como um idealista romântico, embora parecesse reconhecer que ele também fez parte de um capítulo mais sombrio.

“E a pior coisa que podemos fazer hoje é tentar derrubar coisas. Derrubar monumentos sob as vaias da multidão”, disse ele, segundo a agência de notícias estatal Tass.

"Devemos tentar lembrar. Reconhecer tanto nossos sucessos quanto nossos erros. E aprender com eles. Porque, se não lembrarmos da nossa história, estamos fadados a repetir todos os nossos erros."

Quando a própria União Soviética entrou em colapso em 1991, um monumento a Dzerzhinsky em frente à sede da KGB, na Praça Lubyanka, em Moscou, foi derrubado por manifestantes eufóricos.

Foto de arquivo: Manifestantes soviéticos enfurecidos usam guindastes para derrubar uma estátua de Félix Dzerjinski. 23 de agosto de 1991 — Foto: Viktor Korotayev/Reuters

Alguns viram nisso um momento de esperança que daria início a uma nova era, mais livre. Com o tempo, a estátua gigante foi transferida para um parque próximo ao rio Moscou, juntamente com outros símbolos do poder soviético.

Mas alguns dos blogueiros nacionalistas de guerra que têm defendido a guerra da Rússia na Ucrânia afirmaram que agora havia chegado a hora de recolocar a estátua.

"Uma placa é muito boa, mas não é suficiente", escreveu Barba Azul Z, um proeminente blogueiro de guerra com mais de 100 mil seguidores no Telegram. "Tragam Felix de volta à Praça Lubyanka!"

articles.title: Several Russian military aircraft breach South Korea’s air defence zone
articles.summary: South Korea scrambled fighter jets on Tuesday after Russian military aircraft entered its air defence identification zone (ADIZ) over waters between the
articles.body: South Korea scrambled fighter jets on Tuesday after Russian military aircraft entered its air defence identification zone (ADIZ) over waters between the Korean Peninsula and Japan, prompting a brief evacuation alert for residents of an eastern island. Seoul’s military later clarified that the aircraft had not violated the country’s territorial airspace.The Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) said the Russian aircraft flew close to the airspace surrounding Ulleung Island, triggering a military response. Fighter jets were deployed as a precaution to prepare for any contingency, but the Russian planes withdrew without entering South Korean territorial airspace.The clarification came after the interior and safety ministry issued an alert instructing residents of Ulleung Island to move to underground shelters or nearby buildings at around 7:52 am. The warning was withdrawn three minutes later after authorities said the aircraft had moved away from the danger area.The ministry relays military information when issuing public safety alerts. The North Gyeongsang provincial government had also issued a separate warning, initially suggesting that the aircraft could be North Korean.JCS spokesperson Jang Do-young said the Russian aircraft had entered South Korea’s ADIZ and approached the airspace near Ulleung Island, prompting coordination between the military and government agencies over the evacuation warning.Asked whether a communication lapse had led the Safety Ministry to incorrectly report an airspace violation, Jang said the military would need to examine the matter further. He also suggested that the provincial government might have mistakenly issued an alert intended for a military exercise.The military did not disclose the number or types of Russian aircraft involved. Jang said Russian military aircraft had entered South Korea’s air defence identification zone several times this year and that Seoul planned to lodge a protest with Moscow through the Russian military attache.An ADIZ is a designated buffer zone extending beyond a country's territorial airspace, allowing its military to identify, monitor and respond to foreign aircraft approaching its borders. Entry into such a zone does not, by itself, constitute a violation of territorial airspace.No major disruption was reported on Ulleung Island, which has a population of around 9,000. The island was placed on alert in 2022 after North Korea fired more than 20 missiles into the sea amid heightened tensions, with one missile heading towards the island and triggering air raid sirens.The latest incident also recalls a 2019 confrontation, when South Korean fighter jets fired warning shots after a Russian A-50 airborne early warning aircraft entered the country's territorial airspace near Dokdo during a joint Russian-Chinese aerial patrol. Moscow denied violating South Korean airspace at the time.Tuesday’s development comes a week after South Korea deployed fighter jets in response to Russian military aircraft entering its air defence identification zone. Japan also lodged a protest with Moscow on the same day after reporting that two suspected Russian aircraft had entered its airspace off the country's southwestern coast.You use AI every day. articles.title: Larry Ellison loses $10 billion-plus; knocked out of the world's 10-richest men list after Oracle stock falls to 2-year-low,; here's what triggered massive wipe out
articles.summary: Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison has suffered a wealth wipeout of nearly $11 billion after a sharp decline in Oracle’s share price sent his net worth
articles.body: Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison has suffered a wealth wipeout of nearly $11 billion after a sharp decline in Oracle’s share price sent his net worth tumbling and pushed him out of the worlds top 10 richest people, according to a report by Fortune citing Bloomberg data. The fortune of Ellison fell by almost $10.9 billion at the close trading on November 20 as the shares of Oracle continue their prolonged slide. The decline comes as investors grow increasingly concerned about the company’s aggressive spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure, increasing debt levels and negative free cash flow.Oracle shares hit lowest level since January 2024Oracle stock dropped around 7.5% at the end of last week to roughly $102 per share, marking its lowest level since January 2024. The stock has now fallen about 47% over the past year. The latest decline represents a dramatic reversal from September 2025, when Oracle shares reached a record high of $345 amid investor enthusiasm surrounding AI computing demand and the company's growing cloud business.However, sentiment has weakened significantly over the past year as investors scrutinised the costs associated with Oracle's AI expansion strategy.Why Larry Ellison's wealth took such a big hitOne of the biggest reasons of the steep decrease in the personal fortune of Ellison is his sizeable ownership stake in Oracle. The billionaire entrepreneur roughly owns about 40% of the company, which means that any fluctuation in Oracle’s market value will directly impact Ellison’s wealth.As the Oracle shares lost value, the net worth of Larry Ellison fell causing him to slip below Walmart heirs Jim Walton, Rob Walton and Alice Walton on the global rich list. However, despite the multibillion-dollar setback, Ellison is still one of the wealthiest people in the world and his net worth is estimated to be $139 billion, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.Investors worried about AI spending and debtOracle became one of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom as the technology companies rushed to secure computing capacity for the running and training of their artificial intelligence models. Oracle also invested a lot of money in datacenters and cloud infrastructure in order to capitalise the growing demand. However, the investors have always questioned whether the spending made by Oracle is sustainable or not. The investors also raised concerns over the company’s massive investments in AI infrastructure, the increasing debt and the negative cash flow. Oracle’s stock suffered a lot due to all these reasons in recent months. Also, these concerns have overshadowed the optimism which earlier led Oracle shares to record highs.Billionaire fortunes rise and fall with marketsEllison's latest loss highlights how closely the fortunes of many technology billionaires are tied to the performance of their companies' shares. Large stock movements can add or erase billions of dollars in wealth within days.The Oracle founder is far from alone in experiencing dramatic swings in net worth. Fortune noted that Dell Technologies founder Michael Dell saw his wealth surge by more than $120 billion during the height of the AI boom before market fluctuations later reduced those gains. Similarly, Moderna co-founder Robert Langer re-entered the billionaire ranks earlier this year after positive cancer vaccine trial results sent the biotechnology company's stock sharply higher.Fearless legend or grounded realist? articles.title: On the day Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia as CEO, the US blacklists company whose CEO he was romantically linked to
articles.summary: Jensen Huang is back as Nvidia’s CEO. The chipmaker announced his return on Monday, November 23, 12 days after he was ousted from the company he founded.
articles.body: Jensen Huang is back as Nvidia’s CEO. The chipmaker announced his return on Monday, November 23, 12 days after he was ousted from the company he founded. The same day, the US Commerce Department made public a rule adding Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed International to its trade blacklist. According to a report by the news agency Reuters, Alice Huang, who has previously served as Megaspeed’s CEO, has also been identified as the company’s controlling shareholder. She was reported to have had a relationship with the Nvidia co-founder. However, Megaspeed says she left the company in August 2025.Nvidia disclosed in a securities filing that its board reinstated Huang on November 22, a day before the public announcement. Commerce Department cited the risk that advanced US technology could be diverted to China. The designation requires suppliers to seek US government approval for covered shipments to Megaspeed.What US investigators found in the chip supply chainThe US Commerce and Justice departments said that they started investigating Megaspeed in 2024 for potential export-control violations. In May 2025, Commerce Department investigators sought records from Nvidia of sales to Megaspeed, including sales through intermediaries.Nvidia put Megaspeed on its internal sales blocklist the following month. US and Singaporean officials also visited Megaspeed in June to check how the technology was being used and interviewed Alice Huang, then its CEO. The Justice Department subsequently took the lead in the criminal investigation.Megaspeed was a major Nvidia customer, according to Reuters, and Nvidia still listed it in its cloud partner directory when the blacklist move was reported. Cloud providers buy servers equipped with graphics processing units, or GPUs, and rent access to that computing power.The chips can work together to train AI models and run them once they are deployed. For export officials, sales records and on-site checks help establish where the equipment went and who was using it.The Entity List rule covers seven companies across Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand. Its licensing requirements apply to items subject to US export rules, including covered goods, software and technology. That can affect shipments from suppliers outside the United States as well.For Megaspeed, the restrictions could make it harder to expand its computing capacity with new hardware or maintain existing systems with US-origin spare parts and software updates. Regulators will generally deny license applications for the listed companies.What we know about Alice Huang so farThe New York Times reported that US authorities had assessed that Alice Huang passed information to Beijing. Reuters said it could not independently verify that allegation, and China called the accusations “groundless.” Jensen Huang acknowledged an affair in a November 8 statement without naming Alice Huang. Meanwhile, Megaspeed has claimed that it conducted “lawful business.”​Fearless legend or grounded realist? Rate yourself on 11 categories in the Great Indian Confidence Survey – find out in 3–6 min

articles.title: Wedding expenses, mounting debt: UP farmer dies by suicide a day after daughter's engagement
articles.summary: LUCKNOW: A 40-year-old farmer, reportedly struggling with debt and financial difficulties, died by suicide on Sunday (Nov 22), a day after his daughter’s
articles.body: LUCKNOW: A 40-year-old farmer, reportedly struggling with debt and financial difficulties, died by suicide on Sunday (Nov 22), a day after his daughter’s engagement ceremony, in Mod Khurd village under Chirgaon police station limits in Jhansi district.The deceased, identified as Veer Singh Rajput, had reportedly borrowed money to conduct his 19-year-old daughter Shivani’s engagement ceremony and was worried about arranging funds for her wedding, scheduled for May 5, 2027.According to family members, Shivani’s marriage had been fixed with a man from Parichha village in the Baragaon area. On Saturday, the family visited the groom’s house for the traditional ‘phaldan’ ceremony before returning home.Veer Singh’s elder brother, Hariram, said the family was facing financial difficulties and that the farmer had outstanding loans amounting to several lakhs of rupees. He had reportedly taken additional loans to meet the engagement expenses and was worried about arranging money for the remaining wedding expenditure.On Sunday evening, Veer Singh left home, telling family members that he was going to irrigate his agricultural field. When he failed to return for several hours, his family members launched a search and found him in a critical condition in the field.They rushed him to the medical college in Jhansi, where he died during treatment, police said in a statement issued on Tuesday.Chirgaon station house officer Balraj Shahi said the postmortem examination had been completed and the body handed over to the family. Police are examining the circumstances surrounding his death.Veer Singh depended on agriculture to support his family. He had remarried around 11 years ago following the death of his first wife. articles.title: Uttarakhand State Consumer Commission rejects builder's plea to dismiss a house construction complaint, holding that alleged defects and deficiencies in construction fall under consumer law.
articles.summary: DEHRADUN: The Uttarakhand State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has held that engaging a builder to construct a house falls within the ambit of the
articles.body: DEHRADUN: The Uttarakhand State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has held that engaging a builder to construct a house falls within the ambit of the Consumer Protection Act, dismissing a revision petition filed by M/s Sharda Constructions and Developers and its proprietor, Vishw Vijay Singh.The commission found “no illegality or jurisdictional error” in the order passed by the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Dehradun, which had rejected the builders’ application seeking dismissal of a consumer complaint filed by Brij Bhooshan.Bhooshan had filed the complaint on Sept 20, 2021, alleging defects and deficiencies in the construction of his house by the builders. He sought Rs 16.79 lakh, along with 18% annual interest, towards financial losses, Rs 10 lakh for mental agony and another Rs 10 lakh for major construction defects allegedly incapable of being rectified. He also sought litigation costs and other reliefs.The builders filed their written statement on Nov 23, 2021. However, when the matter was listed for their evidence, they moved an application on Feb 17, 2025, under Order 7 Rule 11 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC), seeking rejection of the complaint. They contended that the dispute was essentially a money recovery matter and, therefore, fell outside the jurisdiction of the district commission.Challenging the district commission's Sept 16, 2025, order rejecting their application, the builders also referred to proceedings before the Additional District Judge, Commercial Court, Dehradun, arguing that “no cause of action survived”.Opposing the revision petition, the complainant maintained that the dispute concerned deficiency in service and compensation for losses arising from the alleged deficiencies in construction.The commission observed that while deciding an application under Order 7 Rule 11 of the CPC, the averments made in the complaint must be taken into consideration. It held that the complaint clearly pertained to alleged deficiency in service and that whether such deficiency existed would be determined on the merits of the case.In its Nov 19 order, the state commission also noted that the builders had moved the application nearly two years after the matter had been fixed for their evidence, suggesting that the move was intended to delay the disposal of the complaint. Dismissing the revision petition, it directed both parties to appear before the district commission on Nov 30.Stay updated with the latest Dehradun news. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: A North Carolina mountain tract once slated for more than 170 homes, golf courses and a lake was bought for $4 million, so nearly 1,000 acres of Trout Creek stay forest
articles.summary: A significant conservation effort has secured nearly 1,000 acres of forest land at Trout Creek in North Carolina, previously planned for development with homes and golf courses, ensuring the preservation of its unique wildlife habitats and cold water streams.
articles.body: A patch of forest can disappear quickly once builders move in. That nearly happened at Trout Creek, a mountain tract in Jackson County, North Carolina. In a news release, the Open Space Institute (OSI) said that a nearly 1,000-acre property had been slated for subdivision, with initial development including more than 170 homes, golf courses and a man-made lake. Instead, OSI and Highlands-Cashiers Land Trust purchased it for $4 million and announced its protection on 24 August 2026, so the land remains a forest.A close call for a mountain forestTrout Creek is located in one of the fastest-growing regions of western North Carolina. The land rises from about 2,800 feet to nearly 4,000 feet above sea level. This region is described as one of the last large intact forested areas in the Headwaters District, an area of the southern Appalachians known for its mountains, streams and wildlife habitats. The tract includes montane oak-hickory forest, rich cove forest, rock outcroppings, grassy outcrops and mountain streams. It also borders and partly includes the High Top and Lizzie Mountain Natural Area, which the state's Natural Heritage Program has recognised for its significant conservation value.Why cold water streams matter so muchThe property includes and borders more than five miles of streams and adjacent lands linked to Trout Creek, Little Trout Creek and Bell Conley Branch. According to OSI, leaving this land undeveloped helps the streams continue feeding and recharging cold headwaters that flow into the Little Tennessee River basin. The group added that this supports the water quality of downstream communities. The streams also support southern Appalachian brook trout, which the release called the region's only true native trout. It is regarded as “significantly rare” by the State of North Carolina.Cold water is important for these fish. A 2006 study published in the Transactions of the American Fisheries Society noted that the range of trout within the southern Appalachians, including the brook trout species, is limited by temperature. The authors thought that the warmer climate would restrict them even more. They also warned that warming could cause fragmentation, leaving populations in small isolated patches vulnerable to local extinction.Why higher ground could help wildlife Height can also be a factor. A 2024 study in River Research and Applications looked at 203 streams along nearly 1,000 kilometres of the brook trout’s native range in the southern and central Appalachian Mountains. Its authors, including George Valentine and Yoichiro Kanno, found that the streams most resistant to warming were consistently characterised by southerly latitudes and groundwater input. They also observed that such thermal refugia were more common southward, probably because of higher elevations. However, the study looked at streams across the species’ range rather than Trout Creek specifically, so it cannot show how Trout Creek itself will fare.What happens nextThe tract’s range of elevations provides connected habitat for plants and wildlife as they adjust to warmer temperatures and more extreme weather events. For now, the land remains closed to the public. The two groups hope to hold the property for several years before handing it over to a permanent conservation owner. They hope that hiking, camping and mountain biking will be permitted in the tract when it opens to the public. The Community Foundation of Western North Carolina (CFWNC) helped with the initial due diligence costs while other foundations and individuals supported the project. The project builds on earlier work between the institute and local land trusts, including protection of the 104-acre Peregrine property in 2025 and the 4,400-acre Snowbird Mountain properties.You use AI every day. articles.title: California put $40 million into floodplain plans in 2023; by 2026, River Partners had permits for 6,000 acres, enough to double restored floodplain in the San Joaquin Valley
articles.summary: Learn how California's $40 million investment in floodplain restoration is set to transform 6,000 acres, enhancing flood resilience and supporting wildlife in the San Joaquin Valley.
articles.body: Every few years, a clip of a flooded street goes viral, and most viewers scroll on within seconds. However, that water has to go somewhere, and that question is shaping plans in California. The nonprofit River Partners shared an update in April 2026. In it, the organisation reported that a $40 million grant in 2023 from the California Wildlife Conservation Board helped it finish permits and designs for 6000 acres of floodplain projects in the San Joaquin Valley. The group said the project would double the amount of restored floodplain in the valley. What the $40 million has paid for so farWhat River Partners reported as complete was the planning, not construction. Its scientists and ecologists completed the permits and designs for the 6,000 acres, which is about 2,400 hectares. The organisation described the projects as shovel-ready, meaning work could begin once funding was available. The sites run from Stockton to Bakersfield. One of them is the 675-acre project along eight miles of the Kern River Parkway in Bakersfield, where the plan is to plant 100,000 trees and shrubs. The other is the 4,000-acre project in the San Joaquin River National Wildlife Refuge, 10 miles west of Modesto. The figures were the group's own, and its updates said the work was ready for the next phase, not finished.Why is a floodplain more than empty landFloodplains are flat land next to a river that floods during wet years. Many have been cut off from their rivers by levees over time, and people have farmed or built on them. A 2009 policy paper in Science, ‘Sustainable floodplains through large-scale reconnection to rivers,’ called for reversing some of that. The authors argued that restoring large areas of floodplain farmland could reduce flood risk. They said the land there would be used for activities that could cope with the occasional flooding. Reconnection could make water systems more resilient. The logic is simple. If a river spills out into open country upstream, less water may reach the streets downstream all at once.What happens to the water undergroundFloodwaters can also help refill the aquifers that farms and towns depend on. A study conducted by the California Department of Water Resources looked at the Merced River, which is a 145-mile tributary of the San Joaquin River. In the Merced River Watershed Flood-MAR Reconnaissance Study, they found that an average of 46,500 acre-feet of water per year could be available for recharging aquifers. That is equivalent to 57 million cubic metres of water. The study is based on a century of rainfall, and the department said the estimate could vary. Flood-MAR involves spreading out floodwaters onto the land, where they seep into the soil. This is different from what River Partners is planning, but it suggests a similar advantage. The department also noted that groundwater provides about 40% of California's water supply in a typical year.What still needs to happenRiver Partners says its project can help with flood protection, water supply and wildlife if investment continues. That's an important condition. Permits and designs show that a project can go forward, but they do not guarantee that it will be funded or even built. The group also says it has restored more than 20,000 acres throughout California since 1998. Its Director of Restoration Science, Emma Havstad, said the first step toward adding another 30% was done. All of these claims come from the group doing the work, so as the project gets underway, independent checks will matter. For readers far away from California, the story can show how one funding decision can launch a long-term plan. It also shows how much can still depend on money arriving.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Tawaifs have more shame than your bahus': AIMIM’s Akhtarul Iman lands in controversy over sexist remarks
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: AIMIM Bihar chief Akhtarul Iman on Monday defended his controversial remarks comparing the way brides are dressed and presented at wedding
articles.body: NEW DELHI: AIMIM Bihar chief Akhtarul Iman on Monday defended his controversial remarks comparing the way brides are dressed and presented at wedding receptions to a "tawaif", saying his comments were rooted in Islamic teachings and intended only for Muslims who wish to follow the religion."Tawaifs have more shame than your bahus," Iman said at a gathering.Iman's remarks, made at a public gathering (jalsa), have drawn criticism from political leaders across party lines. He had objected to the practice of dressing brides in traditional finery (solah shringar) and seating them at receptions for relatives and friends to see, arguing that Muslim women should observe 'purdah'.Responding to the criticism, Iman said observing the veil was obligatory (farz) in Islam and that his remarks reflected the teachings of Islamic religious scholars."India has a long tradition of Sufi saints and respect for women. Wearing sindoor is a matter of religious faith, and similarly, Islam requires women to observe purdah and wear hijab. No one should disrespect a religious scholar’s cap or tear a woman’s hijab. My comments were intended only for Muslims who wish to follow Islamic teachings, particularly regarding modesty and interactions between men and women," he told news agency ANI.His remarks triggered sharp reactions from political leaders, with several questioning his views on women's autonomy and the portrayal of women at weddings.Samajwadi Party MP Shiv Pal Singh Patel said the money given to brides at weddings was a form of blessing and that the practice was not limited to any one religion."The money given at weddings is essentially a form of blessing for the daughter; this is a practice found across all religions... The comparison involving Jamila and Sita touches upon the issue of women’s autonomy. It is not as if there is any indecent exposure; if a woman’s face is uncovered and she is adorned, what is wrong with that?.. The regressive notion that a woman must always remain completely covered is something that should not exist... I believe people, including our Muslim brothers, should oppose such thinking," he said.Congress leader Mumtaz Patel also condemned Iman's remarks, saying they were derogatory towards women and did not reflect Islamic teachings."It is very, very disgusting to see the so-called representatives of the community, especially coming from a party like the AIMIM that is supposedly representing Muslims, talk so derogatorily about women. Nowhere does Islam demean women like that. The religion or the culture does not treat women this way. There is a whole narrative being spread where statements like these make Islam a very easy target for everyone to condemn. I condemn this statement, and being a Muslim woman, I think it is absolutely, absolutely wrong..." she said.Uttar Pradesh cabinet minister Om Prakash Rajbhar said different religions had different traditions, but accused leaders like Iman of promoting hatred instead of focusing on issues such as education, healthcare and employment."Different religions have different traditions. These people always talk about hatred. We never hear anyone say, at the very least, that we should talk about educating society, education, health, employment, jobs, peace and brotherhood. Why don't these people talk about these things? They spread this venom in society and conspire to defame it," he said.BJP leader Danish Iqbal also criticised Iman, accusing religious conservatives of trying to impose restrictions on Muslim women's lives in the name of Sharia. He said the Constitution had enabled women to pursue careers across different fields."In this country, regressive maulanas (clerics) have made numerous attempts to impose restrictions on the lives of Muslim women in the name of Sharia. They have sought to enslave them—effectively trying to extinguish their very lives. However, the Constitution of India has empowered Muslim women to such an extent that they are now becoming pilots, doctors, and boxers, excelling across various fields. Despite the persistent efforts of these maulanas—who have consistently used the fear of Sharia to exert control—the Constitution of India has paved the way for Muslim women to reach the pinnacle of success," he said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The renewed alliance between the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The renewed alliance between the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections drew sharp reactions from opposition leaders on Tuesday. Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal accused the two parties of coming together for power and the Congress calling the tie-up opportunistic.The criticism came after Union home minister Amit Shah, BJP president Nitin Nabin and SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal formally announced the alliance at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi. Shah said the two parties would contest all 117 Assembly seats in Punjab, ahead of the 2027 assembly elections, with the SAD to get the chief minister's post.Addressing a joint press conference, Shah said the two parties had decided to fight the Punjab elections together and confirmed that the SAD would rejoin the NDA.“Both the BJP and the Akali Dal have decided to fight the Punjab Assembly elections together and the Akali Dal will also join the NDA from today. This is a great occasion that on Guru Purab the Akali Dal, one of our oldest allies is returning to the NDA,” Shah said.Reacting to the announcement, Kejriwal said the BJP and SAD had repeatedly joined hands and parted ways for political convenience.“Our alliance is with the mothers and daughters of Punjab. Our alliance is with the SC community of Punjab. Our alliance is with the farmers of Punjab. Our alliance is with the traders of Punjab,” Kejriwal said, alleging that political parties come together for power, part ways and reunite.“These people come together for the sake of power, then part ways, and then come together again. We, on the other hand, are working for the development of Punjab. All of Punjab can see how, over the past five years, Bhagwant Mann has worked diligently to try and set things right, to repair the damage inflicted upon Punjab over the last 70–75 years,” he said.“When we spoke to the PM about the expansion of the NDA, he called Sukhbir Badal and said that the NDA is now complete. The Akali Dal and the BJP have a long relationship and this alliance is a symbol of brotherhood and we will move forward together,” Shah said, while announcing the alliance on Tuesday.Meanwhile, Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh termed the alliance a “directionless” tie-up, alleging that the two parties had reunited out of “greed” for power and lacked an agenda for Punjab's development.Reacting to the announcement, Singh told PTI, “The reunion between the SAD and the BJP is only for the greed for power.”“They have no development agenda for Punjab or roadmap for the state's progress. They have joined hands merely for their own development. They have joined hands again with a single motive to capture power in Punjab,” he said, asserting that neither party stood a chance of forming the next government.Singh also asked Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) chief Sukhbir Singh Badal to explain to the people why he had quit the NDA in 2020.AAP leader Jarnail Singh also criticised the reunion, saying, “Zero plus zero will always remain zero. The Akali Dal and the BJP have no future in Punjab, as the people of the state have overwhelmingly rejected both parties for several reasons.”He said people would not forget how more than 700 farmers lost their lives during the protests against the Centre's farm laws. “They will also never forget the sacrilege of the Guru Granth Sahib during the Akali Dal government,” he said.“These two parties, both discredited in the eyes of the people, cannot succeed by joining hands,” Jarnail Singh added.Earlier, Amarinder Singh Raja Warring had also criticised the proposed alliance before its formal announcement. Warring accused Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) leaders Sukhbir Singh Badal and Harsimrat Kaur Badal of misleading voters over their political ties with the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), questioning why the two parties had split in 2020.“Sukhbir Badal and Harsimrat Kaur Badal are trying to fool people. Whenever there was a vote in Parliament on issues such as the Presidential election or the Uniform Civil Code, they would stand with the BJP. But when they came here, they would claim that they had no alliance with the BJP. Why did they break the alliance in the first place?” Warring said.Referring to the Centre's three farm laws, he alleged that the Akali Dal initially supported the legislation before changing its position following protests by farmers.Meanwhile, HM Shah outlined the alliance's priorities, identifying the eradication of drugs and corruption and the strengthening of nationalist forces in Punjab as key goals. He announced a deadline for making the state drug-free.Additionally, “Shah said the BJP and SAD would contest all 117 seats in the Punjab Assembly elections. He also indicated that the chief minister's post would go to the SAD as part of the alliance arrangement.”The BJP and SAD ended their alliance in 2020 after the Akali Dal withdrew from the NDA over the Centre's three farm laws, which were subsequently repealed. The parties contested the 2022 Assembly elections separately.Their electoral fortunes had declined in the years after their split. In 2017, the SAD won 15 seats and the BJP three, while in 2022 the SAD secured three seats and the BJP two. The AAP won 92 seats in 2022.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.summary: Around 20 people were injured when a car bomb exploded in the central Colombian city of Villavicencio, with President Abelardo de la Espriella blaming
articles.body: Around 20 people were injured when a car bomb exploded in the central Colombian city of Villavicencio, with President Abelardo de la Espriella blaming "narco-terrorists" for the attack.The explosion, which occurred on Monday, also destroyed the regional governor's office and damaged several nearby buildings."They have just carried out a bombing attack on the Meta Governor's Office," De la Espriella wrote on X, referring to Colombia's central province of Meta. He confirmed that there were no casualties in the incident."I warn the narco-terrorists responsible: you will answer for every drop of blood you have spilled and every business and property you have destroyed. We will deploy the full power of the state to hunt you down, dismantle your organizations and take you out," he added.No group has claimed responsibility for the attack.De la Espriella, a right-wing leader who took office as Colombia's president in August, has launched a major crackdown on the country's drug trade as left-wing FARC rebels have intensified attacks over the past two years.Also Read: Colombia rocked by car bomb blast a day after new President Abelardo de la Espriella takes chargeBombing coincides with peace deal anniversaryThe bombing came on the eve of the 10th anniversary of the peace agreement signed between the Colombian government and FARC.The deal brought an end to FARC's campaign of bombings, assassinations and hostage-taking. However, violence has surged again over the past two years as remaining guerrilla factions and drug cartels compete for control of the cocaine trade, illegal gold mines and extortion rackets.Also Read: Bomb attack kills 14, injures 38 in Colombia weeks before presidential electionColombia, the world's largest cocaine producer, is now experiencing its worst wave of criminal violence in a decade.De la Espriella has been a vocal critic of the peace process, arguing that former FARC fighters were let off "too lightly" after being spared prison sentences in exchange for admitting to their crimes. He has argued that the arrangement fostered a culture of impunity.Minutes before the blast, the president had criticised the peace agreement, describing it as "false peace" in a post on X."False peace, the squandering of public resources, and corruption scandals during Petro's administration are what have brought Colombia to ruin," he wrote.De la Espriella has vowed to put all remaining armed groups, including breakaway FARC factions, "in a tomb or in prison" and has stepped up military bombardments of their positions.(With AP inputs)You use AI every day. articles.title: LeT, JeM proxies exposed, ISI eyes revival of 19 dormant terror outfits in Jammu and Kashmir
articles.summary: Pakistan's Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) is exploring a shift in its strategy in Jammu and Kashmir, with plans to bring back dormant terror outfits in
articles.body: Pakistan's Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) is exploring a shift in its strategy in Jammu and Kashmir, with plans to bring back dormant terror outfits in the Valley as its existing proxy groups face increased scrutiny from the security agencies, news agency IANS reported.Pakistan's ugly motive is to create a network of revived terror outfits that can operate without any apparent links to established Pakistan-based organisations such as the Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) and Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM), according to officials cited by IANS.The Hafiz Saeed-led LeT has been operating through The Resistance Front (TRF), while Masood Azhar's JeM has been linked to proxy outfits such as the People's Anti-Fascist Front (PAFF), Kashmir Tigers (KT) and Lashkar-e-Mustafa.However, investigations by agencies such as the Jammu and Kashmir Police and the National Investigation Agency (NIA) have increasingly exposed the links between these outfits and their parent organisations. The agencies have gathered evidence indicating that the different names are being used to mask the involvement of the LeT and JeM.An official told IANS that the ISI has now advised these groups to reconnect with former members of terror organisations that have been inactive in Jammu and Kashmir for years.Several of these outfits emerged during the 1990s and early 2000s, when militancy was at its peak in the Valley. However, as the ISI concentrated its operations around the LeT, JeM and Hizbul Mujahideen, many smaller groups gradually became inactive.Some ran out of funds, while others lost their operatives to security force operations, the official said.19 dormant terror outfits on ISI radarAccording to data cited by IANS, Jammu and Kashmir currently has 10 active terror groups, while 19 outfits remain inactive. Among the dormant organisations are the Kashmir Jehad Force (KJF) and Tehrik-e-Jihad (TeJ).An Intelligence Bureau official said the ISI is likely to focus on locating former members of these groups and encouraging them to rebuild their networks."These members would be told to look out for potential recruits and then revive these terror groups. There would be no direct link between these groups and the existing terror outfits. This helps the ISI in covering its tracks when an investigation into a terror attack is launched," the official said.A major consideration behind the proposed strategy is that several of these organisations are homegrown rather than Pakistan-based. Their revival could make it more difficult for investigators to establish direct links with established terror outfits operating from across the border, the report said.Local recruitment, infiltration among key concernsThe ISI is also expected to draw on the experience of former members in areas such as recruitment and logistics. Although many of them are now older, officials believe their knowledge of local networks could prove useful in rebuilding the outfits.The agency is likely to focus on recruiting local youth, while Pakistan continues to explore ways to increase infiltration into Jammu and Kashmir through multiple routes, an official told IANS.Another official said the ISI is keen to restore militant activity in the Valley. However, the recent killing of Lashkar commander Lateef Bhat has dealt a setback to its plans and could delay efforts to revive terror networks for some time.The revived groups could be used for both ground operations and information warfare, including disinformation and propaganda campaigns, officials said.This would require security agencies to tackle not only possible terror operations but also coordinated attempts to influence public opinion through propaganda, adding to the security challenges in Jammu and Kashmir, the report said.You use AI every day. articles.title: An Australian woman's Doberman fell nearly six metres into an abandoned mineshaft while chasing a rabbit and was pulled out alive by rescuers; remarkably, another of her dogs had needed a similar rescue years earlier
articles.summary: The thing about magic is that it can be found in the most unexpected of places.
articles.body: The thing about magic is that it can be found in the most unexpected of places. Sometimes, it even comes with four legs, a wagging tail and a rather unfortunate habit of chasing rabbits. In Western Victoria, Australia, a rabbit chase by a dog named Magic ended in a frightening situation after she fell into an abandoned mineshaft on Monday, November 16.According to ABC News, in a report dated November 20, 2026, the Doberman was reportedly trapped nearly six metres below ground before a specialist rescue team was called in to bring her back to safety. Fortunately, following the team's rescue efforts, Magic was reunited with her owner, and no injuries were reported.Rescue operationThe incident required the involvement of Fire Rescue Victoria (FRV), whose specialist high-angle rescue team was brought in to retrieve the stranded dog. Unlike a situation where an animal can simply be reached and lifted out, a deep and narrow mineshaft presents a rather different challenge, requiring rescuers to carefully navigate the space before they can bring the animal to the surface.A member of the rescue team had to enter the shaft, secure a harness around Magic and help prepare her for the journey upwards. The high-angle team then hoisted her nearly six metres to safety, bringing an end to what could have been a considerably more distressing situation for both the dog and her owner. While the circumstances surrounding her fall were certainly frightening, the operation was successful, and she was brought out of the mineshaft alive. However, what made the incident notable was not simply that a dog had fallen into an abandoned mine, but that this was not the first time the same owner had experienced something similar.A similar case beforeABC News reported how the rescue seemed like a case of déjà vu for Invermay Country Fire Authority (CFA) firefighter Daryl Rowe, who was reminded of a similar operation. As it turned out, another dog belonging to the same owner had also fallen into a mineshaft approximately 10 years earlier and required rescuers to intervene.Speaking to ABC News, Rowe described the situation as a familiar one, with the owner having experienced an almost identical predicament years earlier. Although it might seem like an extraordinary coincidence for the same household to have two dogs fall into abandoned mineshafts, the firefighter explained that the surrounding region makes such incidents less surprising than they might initially appear."There are thousands of mineshafts up there," Rowe told ABC News, explaining that they are scattered throughout the area. He added that rescuers had encountered situations involving both animals and people falling into these openings, requiring emergency teams to arrange their safe removal.The hidden dangers of Ballarat's mining landscapeThe Ballarat region has a long association with gold mining, particularly dating back to the historic gold rush of the 1850s. Although much of that mining activity belongs to the past, its physical remnants have not entirely disappeared. Disused mineshafts remain scattered across the landscape, posing challenges for local authorities and emergency services alike.One of the difficulties, as Rowe explained, is that identifying and securing every abandoned shaft is far from simple. Locating each one is a major undertaking, while the expense involved in covering every opening would also be prohibitive. In his conversation with ABC News, he pointed out that it was not practical to prevent people from enjoying walks through the bush simply because these hazards existed.Some mineshafts can be identified through a slight depression in the ground, but this alone does not make them easy to recognise. An opening can be concealed by its surroundings, making it difficult to distinguish from the natural landscape.For this reason, Rowe advised visitors unfamiliar with the region to remain on formed pathways, designated bicycle tracks and roadways rather than wandering through unfamiliar sections of bushland. The recommendation is particularly relevant in an area where the remnants of historic mining activity can still be encountered.Magic's rescue, therefore, is not just an account of an adventurous dog getting into trouble and being fortunate enough to find help. It also draws attention to an unusual hazard that continues to exist in parts of western Victoria, even decades after the mining activity that created it has ended.You use AI every day.
