articles.title: ‘26 seats’ to start with: Akhilesh strikes a poetic note on SP-Congress alliance talks
articles.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Tuesday wove a poetic verse around the ongoing seat-sharing talks with the Congress for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh
articles.body: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Tuesday wove a poetic verse around the ongoing seat-sharing talks with the Congress for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, saying the process had begun with an offer of 26 seats and would move forward through mutual understanding."जीतनेवाली पहली ‘26 सीटों’ से हुई है शुरुआत, मिलजुलकर समझदारी से और आगे बढ़ेगी बात" (The winning start has been made with the first ‘26 seats’; working together wisely, things will move forward), Akhilesh said in the verse shared amid negotiations between the two INDIA bloc allies.The alliance between the two parties remains intact, and the seat-sharing arrangement is expected to be finalised in the coming meetings, Congress sources said on Tuesday. The next round of talks is likely to take place on November 27.Earlier in the day, Akhilesh said the primary objective of an alliance was to win elections and that discussions were under way to assess the winnability of candidates in each constituency.Speaking to reporters in Lucknow, the SP chief said senior leaders entrusted with the negotiations were actively engaged in the process, but it was too early to disclose details of the proposed arrangement."Regarding the ongoing discussions, our party's senior leaders, along with those entrusted by the party to handle these talks, are currently engaged in the process. What exactly is being discussed? How many seats are being agreed upon, and how many could the other party potentially win? These matters are under consideration, so it is difficult to say anything definitive right now. Alliances are formed with the sole objective of winning; the purpose of an alliance is victory," Akhilesh said.Emphasising the need to counter Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), he said the SP was prepared to make adjustments to secure an electoral victory."The Samajwadi Party is committed to making adjustments and accommodations because the battle ahead is significant. When the goal is to win, and we must win, especially against a political 'machine' like the BJP, we have to prepare accordingly and make the right decisions," he said.Akhilesh also raised questions about the electoral process and the functioning of the Election Commission of India (ECI)."Constitutional bodies have a duty to act fairly, yet questions are being raised about this very body. It is now being suggested that the BJP is planning to add approximately 3 crore votes. Furthermore, regarding the warehouses where EVMs are stored, who are the engineers tasked by the ECI with maintaining these machines? We are told that the machines are being 'serviced,' but no one knows who these engineers actually are," he said.SP MP Rajeev Rai confirmed that the party had offered 26 seats to the Congress ahead of the second round of negotiations."We will hold discussions regarding the number of seats. We have offered them 26 seats," Rai said.SP Rajya Sabha MP Ram Gopal Yadav also said the proposal had been conveyed to the Congress during Monday's meeting and that discussions would continue."Whatever had to be said in the meeting, we said yesterday. We have offered them our 26 seats, and today we are going to hold talks again," he said.Congress leaders also described the negotiations as positive. AICC in-charge for Uttar Pradesh Rajendra Pal Gautam expressed confidence that the seat-sharing arrangement would be finalised in the next two meetings."We are heading in the right direction. In the next two meetings, everything will be done. Discussions have been held on several seats. Discussions have been held on every single seat on the basis of data. The discussions are heading in a positive direction. Both parties are going ahead with a positive mindset. 403 is a big number; discussions have been held on more than half of them. We will wind this up in the next two meetings. Our alliance will be a done deal. We will make the announcement soon," Gautam said.Congress Legislature Party leader in Uttar Pradesh Aradhana Misra 'Mona' also described the first round of talks as positive and said further discussions would be held before the alliance was formally announced."We discussed seats in the meeting. It was a positive discussion, and only one round of discussion has been concluded so far. The second round of discussion will be held soon, and if needed, we will come together again. The exercise will continue until we announce the alliance positively," she said.The first round of formal seat-sharing negotiations between the two parties was held in New Delhi on Monday at the official residence of senior Congress MP Pramod Tiwari. Leaders from both parties took part in the discussions.In the 2022 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, which the parties contested separately, the SP won 111 of the 347 seats it contested, while the Congress secured two of the 399 seats it fielded candidates in.In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the two parties contested together as part of the INDIA bloc.
